newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends range-bound after NYMEX-led spurt.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends range-bound after NYMEX-led spurt.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures rallied to session highs in late dealing, pulled up by short-covering on the expiring April NYMEX contract, but fell back into mid-range at the close, dealers said.
May Brent closed 13 cents off at $20.19 a barrel, 36 cents below the session high posted in the last 20 minutes of trade.
"There was no obvious explanation other than (short) liquidation on the (NYMEX) April contract," said a broker, referring to the late strength.
NYMEX April crude expired up six cents at $22.10 a barrel, pulling the prompt April/May spread out by five cents.
Brent had spent much of the session trapped in a range between last Friday's low of $20.07 and $20.50, Tuesday's high.
But a finish below $20.32, Thursday's closing level, and the relatively light volumes suggested further losses could be looming, dealers said.
"The trade is still not convinced, partly because there's a lot of oil in Europe," said a broker.

North Sea benchmark Dated Brent traded again on Thursday at a deep discount to the forward market, although there was some evidence that differentials for other regional crudes could be ready for a move higher.
News some refiners in northwest Europe were restoring crude runs to normal levels after recent reductions due to poor margins was providing mild support, traders said.

Technical analysts said both the early downward correction on Brent and the subsequent recovery were expected, given a lacklustre close Wednesday and the ability of the May contract to hold above $19.61 a barrel, keeping intact the uptrend channel in place since the beginning of the month.
Earlier, IPE April gas oil closed at $173.00 a tonne, down $2 after hovering in a $172-$174 holding pattern in thin volumes. --Mark Thompson, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7930
